title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Following the Cash — 10-Year Financials & Earnings Quality
question: How clean is SK hynix's cash conversion across a full 10-year memory cycle, how strong is the balance sheet today, and what non-operating items distort 2026 net income?

epigraph.quote: Profitability is an accounting opinion; free cash flow after fab capex is the only truth in semiconductors.
epigraph.author: Institutional Memory Underwriting Principle

web_blocks.html: From FY2016 through FY2025, SK hynix revenue grew more than fivefold from KRW 17.20T to KRW 97.15T [1, 7]. In the first three quarters of FY2026 alone, revenue surged to KRW 236.52T [2, 3]. Yet the path was volatile. Operating profit hit KRW 20.84T (51.5% margin) in FY2018, fell to KRW 2.71T (10.0%) in FY2019, and recovered to KRW 12.41T in FY2021. It then plunged to a KRW -7.73T loss (-23.6%) in FY2023 before rebounding to KRW 47.21T in FY2025 and KRW 83.33T (79.7%) in Q3 2026 [1, 2, 7].

web_blocks.takeaway: Operating profit is the cleanest measure of core earnings power: Q2 2026 net income of KRW 93.92T exceeded operating profit of KRW 60.54T due to one-time Kioxia stake valuation gains, which must be stripped out of recurring run-rate underwriting.

web_blocks.html: Forensic review flags Q2 2026 net income (KRW 93.92T) as an accounting outlier. SK hynix booked non-operating valuation gains on its Kioxia stake in that quarter [3]. As a result, net income exceeded operating profit (KRW 60.54T) by more than KRW 33 trillion [3]. By contrast, Q3 2026 operating profit of KRW 83.33T yielded KRW 39.78T in net profit after taxes and adjustments [2]. Analysts must focus on operating profit, EBITDA, and operating cash flow rather than headline net income.

web_blocks.title: Cash conversion, balance-sheet repair, and capital intensity

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion during the 2024–2025 upcycle has been genuine, not paper-driven. In FY2025, SK hynix generated ~$37.36B in operating cash flow (~KRW 53.28T) against KRW 42.95T in net income [1]. That >120% conversion ratio was aided by KRW 13.93T in non-cash depreciation [1]. Even after ~KRW 28.60T ($20.06B) in capex, free cash flow topped KRW 24.68T ($17.30B). Cash and short-term investments rose from KRW 14.2T at end-2024 to ~KRW 35.14T at end-2025, while debt fell to ~KRW 22.25T–24.76T. That flipped SK hynix to net cash with Debt/Equity at 0.08 and ROIC at 71.84%.

Equity dilution has been modest relative to earnings scale. The July 2026 Nasdaq ADS offering added cross-border equity to pre-fund Yongin, Cheongju P&T7, and EUV tools [4, 5]. Solvency is not the risk—SK hynix holds ample liquidity. The real watchpoint is capital-intensity creep. With annual capex at 29%–30% of peak sales, any cyclical revenue drop forces management to cut capex fast or burn cash.

web_blocks.mechanism: Following a cloud-driven DRAM supercycle in FY2017–FY2018 where gross margins and operating cash flow surged, Micron ramped multi-year fab capex just as hyperscale customers entered an inventory digestion pause in 2019.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Micron suffered sharp revenue contraction and severe operating-margin compression across FY2019–FY2020 as DRAM pricing normalized, while multi-year fab capital expenditures remained elevated.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even structurally healthier memory oligopolies see free cash flow compress sharply when multi-year fab commitments collide with a customer inventory pause. SK hynix's >50% LTA coverage for 2027–2028 is a stronger shock absorber than Micron had in 2018, but it does not eliminate capex rigidity.

web_blocks.takeaway: SK hynix used its 2024–2025 cash surge to erase downturn net debt, building KRW 35.14T in cash and short-term investments against KRW 22.25T–24.76T in total debt while funding KRW 28.60T in annual capex.

web_blocks.html: The balance-sheet bridge from FY2023 to FY2025 provides the strongest fundamental defense against historical memory-failure base rates. At the 2023 trough, borrowings climbed near KRW 29.5T as SK hynix absorbed -KRW 9.14T in consolidated net losses and Solidigm capital impairment [7, 20]. Two years later, cash and short-term investments reached ~KRW 35.14T against KRW 22.25T–24.76T in total debt, dropping Debt/Equity to 0.08 and lifting ROIC to 71.84% and ROE to 93.70%. That net-cash buffer—reinforced by the July 2026 Nasdaq ADS raise—ensures SK hynix can fund Yongin and Indiana without jeopardizing solvency even if margins normalize sharply from 2026 peaks.

book_paragraphs: In Chapter 6, you and I put on our forensic accountant hats. A company can report dazzling net income for one quarter, but only ten years of cash flow and balance-sheet numbers tell you whether owners actually get to keep the money.

Look at SK hynix's ten-year record from 2016 to 2026, and start by spotting the accounting trap in Q2 2026. In that quarter, SK hynix reported KRW 60.54 trillion in operating profit, yet net income jumped to KRW 93.92 trillion. Why? Non-operating valuation gains on its Kioxia investment. You and I never capitalize one-time investment markups into recurring earnings power; we anchor on operating profit and operating cash flow.

When we do that, the underlying cash engine in FY2025 is still extraordinary. Operating cash flow hit roughly $37.36 billion—more than 120% of net income—because $9.77 billion of non-cash depreciation flows back into cash. After spending $20.06 billion on fabs and EUV tools, SK hynix banked $17.30 billion in free cash flow.

That cash transformed a balance sheet that looked stretched in 2023. By the end of 2025, cash and short-term investments reached KRW 35.14 trillion against roughly KRW 22.3 trillion to KRW 24.8 trillion in total debt, putting SK hynix into a solid net-cash position before its July 2026 Nasdaq ADS offering.

Let's look closely at the balance sheet repair between 2023 and 2025, because that is where financial durability is won or lost. At the bottom of the 2023 memory winter, SK hynix carried nearly KRW 29.5 trillion in borrowings against roughly KRW 9 trillion in cash, while Solidigm's equity had turned negative from KRW 7.3 trillion in cumulative losses.

Two years of HBM cash flow flipped that script completely. By the end of 2025, cash and short-term investments had swelled nearly fourfold to KRW 35.14 trillion while total debt fell toward KRW 22.3 trillion to KRW 24.8 trillion. Debt-to-equity dropped to just 0.08, and return on invested capital hit 71.84%.

That net-cash fortress—plus the fresh equity from the July 2026 Nasdaq ADS offering—means SK hynix is no longer the fragile, over-leveraged Hyundai spin-off of 2001 or the stretched borrower of 2008. Even if the next memory cycle compresses margins from 80% back down toward 20% or 30%, the balance sheet can absorb the shock without forced asset sales.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Depreciation Is Not Free Cash in Fabs
book_callouts.text: In FY2025, SK hynix added back $9.77 billion of depreciation to reach $37.36 billion in operating cash flow—and then spent $20.06 billion on new capex, more than double depreciation. In leading-edge memory, depreciation is a real economic cost because EUV tools and cleanrooms must be replaced every node.

book_subsections.title: What Micron's 2018–2020 Cycle Teaches Us
paragraphs: To see how quickly cash conversion can tighten, look at Micron Technology between 2018 and 2020. At the 2018 cloud-DRAM peak, Micron earned high operating margins and committed heavy multi-year capital into new fabs. When cloud customers paused orders in 2019 and 2020, revenue contracted sharply and operating margins compressed while fab capex kept rolling.

SK hynix today has two protections Micron lacked in 2018: a net-cash balance sheet and multi-year HBM4 Long-Term Agreements covering over half of 2027–2028 capacity. Even so, its massive Yongin and Indiana buildouts mean fixed depreciation will rise every year, so free cash flow remains sensitive to wafer utilization.

book_subsections.title: Separating Core Earnings from Non-Operating Noise in 2026
paragraphs: Before we close Pass 1, remember the forensic rule for 2026 earnings: never treat Q2 2026 net income of KRW 93.92 trillion as a recurring quarterly run rate. That number was inflated by over KRW 33 trillion of non-operating valuation gains tied to SK hynix's Kioxia stake.

Instead, look at operating profit: KRW 37.61 trillion in Q1, KRW 60.54 trillion in Q2, and KRW 83.33 trillion in Q3 2026. That trajectory—combined with >120% operating cash conversion in FY2025—proves the core HBM and server memory engine is generating real cash, even though cyclical capex will always claim a large slice of it.
